_comment: The KIT's own claims, run by `doctor.ps1 -Kit`. ${KIT} is this checkout; relative paths are kit-relative. These are facts about the kit tree, never about any adopter's disk. Type reference: SPEC 5.2 / tools/MANUAL.md.

claims.why: Kit LAW.md is GENERATED from law.json (C5). A hand edit to LAW.md drifts the grades away from the mechanisms that justify them; this claim makes that drift a RED run instead of a quiet lie. Compared as bytes after CRLF->LF only.

C6, F2: the personal layer never enters the kit. Whole-word, case-insensitive, scoped to text files. The allow table is span-based: the author slug is permitted in exactly the files that must carry it, and nowhere else; a bare first or last name is a leak everywhere. This file is excluded because it is the word list itself; the self-test file may carry the slug only, because it is the fixture that proves the span rule. The state folder is generated by the Doctor itself, gitignored, and records remote URLs, so it is excluded: a scan that trips on its own output is noise.

F15, C4: a hook that never reaches its first line (pwsh missing, Mark-of-the-Web refusal, parse error) is invisible to every in-body check. Runs the guard exactly as hooks.json registers it with a harmless synthetic tool call; it must exit 0 and reply with nothing or JSON.
Same observation for the fence: the only pre-body check there is. Exit 0 and an empty or JSON reply on a harmless call.
F4: the entry path must never load silently empty. SessionStart passes only with exit 0 AND non-empty stdout, because stdout is the carrier for the entry path.

The subagent hook (DES-11) is registered for the Agent tool and must start: run as hooks.json registers it with a harmless synthetic call, exit 0, reply with nothing or JSON. A non-Agent payload must pass through silently.
